decisions.reason: The n>=2 energy proof invokes the first Green identity, whose Statement assumes AC_omega. Added that exact premise for n>=2; the n=1 mean-value and endpoint-normal argument remains choice-free. Zero continuous gradient energy forces zero gradient on each component and hence constancy. No direct item consumer exists; the home page already explicitly propagates Countable Choice.

The Definition explicitly defines a kernel candidate and defers the n>=2 Dirac identity to its subsequent theorem; the descriptive title does not assume that identity in the local proof. The polar integrals R^2/(2(n-2)) and -R^2 log(R)/2+R^2/4 establish exactly the claimed local integrability, with omega_1=2pi. Step 1.2 separately proves the one-dimensional slope-jump identity. No circular assertion or repair is needed.

The cited kernel item actually proves -Phi_1 second derivative = delta_0 in Proof step 1.2 by two half-line integrations by parts. F2 accurately says it separately verifies this fact, even though the abbreviated Statement does not export the identity. Moreover the interval proof independently computes slopes (b-y)/L and -(y-a)/L, their jump -1, and the distributional identity in steps 4.1-6.1. Its affine correction uses only the explicit profile; the rejection is a false positive.

The title omitted the minus sign although the Statement and full excision proof establish -Delta T_Phi=delta_0. On the inner annular sphere the outward normal is -omega, giving positive unit flux; the Phi times normal-test derivative term is O(epsilon) or O(epsilon|log epsilon|), and local integrability removes the omitted ball. Translation gives delta_y. Corrected only the title; this nonfatal display defect changes no Statement/Definition or proof obligation.

F15 cited a theorem explicitly restricted to null subsets of R, while step 5.1 takes a union of exceptional subsets of R^n. Replaced that load-bearing citation with the published general countable-subadditivity theorem and derived lambda_n(union E_m)<=sum lambda_n(E_m)=0 explicitly. The uniform local kernel bound licenses Tonelli/Fubini for compact L1 data, the translated Dirac pairing gives -Delta T_Nf=T_f, and uniform derivative bounds away from K give smooth harmonicity. No Statement/Definition changed.

The displayed index range 1<=i,j<=n conflicts with the actual coordinate set 0,...,n-1. Corrected it to 0<=i,j<n; this is a nonfatal indexing defect because the coordinate-independent Hessian calculation proves the identical formula for every valid coordinate. Checked the cutoff limits, the -delta_ij/n sphere correction, integrability of r^(alpha-1), and the far-region d integral of r^(alpha-2), requiring 0<alpha<1. The full C2,alpha claim is retained.

F22 falsely asserted existence of coordinate e_1 for n=1 although the basis is indexed below n. Restricted this local fact to n>=2, already the example hypothesis, and identified e_1 as coordinate 1 rather than the first vector. Also restored omega_(n-1) in the intermediate polar normalization and stated the compact-support majorant correctly; final integral formulas were already correct. The reflection proves radiality; ball flux gives u prime=-r^(1-n) integral_0^r s^(n-1)rho, whose magnitude is O(r) at zero.
